blocks.content: We are excited to invite you to our Marshall Mile and Family Picnic on FRIDAY, May 8th! We look forward to seeing many of you there to help us celebrate a wonderful day of fitness, fun, and community.Important Details:No Backpacks: Please have your child come to school without a backpack on this day.Early Dismissal Procedures: If you plan to sign your child out after the event, please note that students will not return to their classrooms to retrieve any belongings.Marshall Mile:The event will take place in and around the parking lot.Spectators are welcome to watch from the grass areas or along the perimeter of the parking lot.After completing the mile, all students will return to the building with their teacher - Students will be able to be signed out from the picnic.Family Picnic:Families staying for the picnic should walk through the parking lot to the swing set side of the playground to meet their child.Students may purchase a picnic lunch in the cafeteria.Families are encouraged to bring a picnic lunch for themselves and/or their child.Seating will be limited — we recommend bringing a blanket or chairs.Student Sign-Out:Staff will be stationed by the door nearest the swing set to assist with signing students out.After signing your child out, you will receive a GREEN slip. This slip must be visible to staff and will indicate that your child has been properly signed out.Please do not go to the office to sign your child out.We are looking forward to a great day with our students and families! Thank you for your cooperation and support in helping the day run smoothly.Below are the times for the Run and Picnic.

title: Tips for Improving Student Reading Comprehension
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
NOTES 

FROM 

TITLE 

TALK 

NOTES FROM TITLE TALK

Does your student understand what they are reading? A reader needs to understand what they are reading; simply reading the words is not enough. A good way to know if your student is understanding what they are reading is by asking questions. Questions about the story elements (characters, setting, events, etc.) let you know if your student is comprehending the text. Some questions you may want to ask:Who is the main character? Where does the story take place? (Setting: place and time)What is the problem? How was the problem solved?Activities: Ask your student to retell the story. Have your student draw a picture of the story. In Reading Corner, we are using the UFLI curriculum. Here is a parent resource for you to look at!Parent reading help K-3If you need help with any of these activities, please reach out to your student’s Reading Corner teacher.

summary: Parents can help assess reading comprehension by asking questions about story elements like characters, setting, and plot. **Suggested activities**: have students retell the story or draw pictures about what they read. The Reading Corner program uses the **UFLI curriculum** and offers a [parent resource guide](Parent reading help K-3). Contact your student's Reading Corner teacher for additional support.

As part of our celebration, students will have the opportunity to invite a VIP (Very Important Pirate) to join them during their scheduled library time. VIPs may be parents, grandparents, special family members, or other important adults in your child’s life.During this special visit, VIPs and students will:Read together (bring a favorite book from home or choose one from our library collection)Complete a fun directed drawing activityPlay a gameWe kindly ask all VIPs to sign up using this link so we can plan accordingly. (If you have more than one student, please fill one out for each student.) Additionally, any grown-up who would like to attend must have a completed volunteer application on file prior to coming in. The form can be emailed directly to Mrs. Jones or returned to your child’s teacher. If you have already completed a volunteer application and have one on file with the school, you are all set—no need to complete another one.On the day of your visit, please arrive 5–10 minutes before your child’s scheduled library time. VIP’s will need to bring an ID and sign in at the office. A staff member will greet VIPs and walk the group up to the library when it is time for the class to begin.Thank you for partnering with us and helping make Right to Read Week a memorable and meaningful experience for our students!

We look forward to welcoming our VIPs aboard for this exciting week of literacy fun!If you have any questions, please feel free to contact Mrs. Jones @ joness@talawanda.org or 513-273-3600.Stephanie JonesPrincipal
